Continuing: for P7–P17, the statement “There is a knight above me” is true exactly when some knight is above them. If any of P3–P6 is a knight, then P7–P17 are all knights. If P3–P6 were all liars, then P3’s statement would be true (since P4 is a liar below), impossible. So P7–P17 are all knights.

Now P6 says “There is a liar below me,” but P7–P17 are all knights, so P6’s statement is false; hence P6 is a liar. Then P5’s statement is true because P6 is a liar below, so P5 is a knight. Similarly P4 and P3 are knights.

Thus the knights are P3, P4, P5, and P7–P17:  
\(3+11=14\).

\boxed{14}
